The Council of Sagus Cliffs meets on the sun-swept square at the top of the crag, overlooking the broad waters of Garravia Sound. Enormous synth slabs pave the square, and the tips of ancient space-faring vessels protrude from the ground, now repurposed as public buildings. The Order of Truth maintains its small, independent headquarters inside one of the starships, and emissaries from strange places meet in the Red Thicket, where their words cannot be overheard.

Sagus Cliffs is one of the oldest human cities in Greater Garravia, built upon the ruins of more ancient metropolises. It occupies the headland overlooking Garravia Sound, with switchbacks and cutouts in the bluffs creating broad avenues that wind down to the harbors. Humanity has filled the old streets with their own ramshackle constructions, building wherever they can find a place to stake their claim. Strange towers and remnants of lost worlds pock the city here and there, and old machines still hum in the artificial caverns beneath the city. It is in these caverns that you see the city's true geological strata – the detritus of forgotten times.  Some neighborhoods close to the cliffs' edges are in danger of falling into the bay below. Every year, the city loses a little ground and a few more lives.

Once the heart of the Sagus Protectorate, the city's fortunes have slipped, its territory shrinking to a small pocket of land surrounding the city.

"Girar, the handsome young human Aeon Priest, whirled around, holding his quarterstaff before him. The mob of disgusting, slobbering, diseased, ignorant mutants and baby-stealing visitants closed like a dripping fist around him and the innocent children he had sworn to protect.

'For Midgard and the future of humanity!' shouted Angule, champion of humans everywhere and the last hope of kindness and decency in the Ninth World. She charged into the clustered hordes of monsters, slashing left and right. The creatures felt no pain for they had no souls.

Humming and Hiding - The Secrets of the Labyrinth of Sound

"I will not tell you *why* I found myself lost within the crumbling tower of Kasmus Gol. Nor will I speak on the state I found myself in, or who was with me. Promises were made in the spiraling depths of the Labyrinth of Sound. Promises I intend to keep.

Instead, I will tell you of my escape from that echoing prison. 'But Krasha,' you might say. 'I know enough of the Labyrinth to say that it is but a dark room, navigated by music rather than crude movement. Furthermore, it is deserted! One will not, for example, stumble over bands of thieving murden there, as you did in your thrilling account of "The Crossing of Deep Vormask."'

To this, I respectfully ask you to close this book and explore the Labyrinth on your own, bereft of my guidance. You will find the melody-scarred bones of my friends still cooling there. You will stumble over grotesque evidence of the choices I made to escape those lightless halls. And you will see how far your rudimentary knowledge will take you.

Otherwise, remain silent, and read on."

This moss-covered pebble looks almost ordinary, and if it were lying on the ground, it would be difficult to spot. But the moss shifts in unexpected ways, and the pebble vibrates as it does. If held against the skin, the moss latches on and is absorbed, providing powerful resuscitating energies. These pebbles are found by diving into the waters around Sagus Cliffs, perhaps grown by an unknown interaction with the surrounding numenera. The moss was further treated and refined, detached and reattached to the pebble, a process that amplifies the interaction between the two objects and increases the effects when the moss is absorbed.

Exit Torment: Tides of Numenera

Thank you for participating in this Alpha Systems Test of Torment: Tides of Numenera. This early glimpse of the game is exclusive to you as one of our Alpha Systems Testers. In this slightly updated version of the initial sequence, we made assorted minor changes to address much of your feedback. It has not fundamentally changed, but you'll notice a number of minor improvements. Please see the Release Notes for more information. Additional feedback is welcome!

Welcome to Torment: Tides of Numenera's beta. This build will take you through Sagus Cliffs, which is the first major location in Torment. The story we've created is reactive, detailed and set in a world unlike any other. We encourage you to play multiple times to get a sense of how your choices can change your path through the Ninth World.

This latest version comes with thousands of changes, many directly from our community's feedback and suggestions.
Here's an overview of the biggest:

- 4K backgrounds
- Two new party members available
- New UI artwork and design
- Added merchants and trading
- Character system and Crisis mechanics updates
- Early game sequence reworked
- Improved background art, visual effects and sound effects

Torment is still a ways from final release, and we will continue to polish and improve the game. We encourage you to use the Feedback button at the top of the screen to relay your thoughts or bug reports, as well as on the forums. The messages and comments from our backers and fans are invaluable, and we will be reading them.

Known issues:

- Balance is at an early pass
- Random text errors appear in conversations and barks
- Some side quests may break

Whether you are playing for the first time, or a returning player checking out the newest version, we hope you enjoy your journey...
